placements.why: The envelope's content is an organizational decision about deployment process authority — a mandatory gate, its scope, and its owner. No existing strata or narrative structure covers deployment process governance, so this category is minted to hold the leaves this content calls for.
placements.title: governing how releases ship through mandatory controls
placements.frame: What mandatory controls and gates govern deployment to staging and production?

placements.title: past failure becomes the whole reason for a mandatory gate
placements.frame: Is the authority of this control grounded in a specific prior incident rather than abstract policy?
placements.why: src-1 declares the signed-manifest gate as now-required; src-2 supplies the causal justification — two unsigned artifacts reaching staging is 'the whole reason for the gate.' src-4 restates the gate as a decision-record item. Together they carry a theme about gate authority deriving from a concrete past failure, a subject future envelopes could continue to feed with other incident-justified controls.

placements.title: a gate's scope and ownership ratified as a decision record
placements.frame: How does a mandatory control get formalized into scope and ownership through a ratified decision?
placements.why: src-4 restates the gate requirement, src-5 extends its scope to staging and production, and src-6 assigns ownership to Quinton Fairweather — all as settled decision-record artifacts performing the act of formalizing an operational control's boundaries and accountability. This is a thematic container for how mandatory controls get ratified into scope and ownership, distinct from the incident-justification theme.
